title: DFA chief mum on Pax Silica deal signing during Trump's PH visit
summary: Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro on Monday declined to say whether an agreement on the proposed Pax Silica initiative would be signed during the upcoming visit of US President Donald…

blocks.text: Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro on Monday declined to say whether an agreement on the proposed Pax Silica initiative would be signed during the upcoming visit of US President Donald Trump to the Philippines.

“Let me reiterate, my mandate here is to reflect on the meetings that happened today. If there’s any question on diplomatic state-to-state Philippine discussions, then we’ll wait for that day, or perhaps we just have to have the discussions first,” Lazaro said in a press conference on the sidelines of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits.
“Because I’m doing it on a day-to-day basis,” she added.

US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton earlier said there was no scheduled announcement on the Pax Silica initiative during the ASEAN Summit. He said decisions would be made in “full consultation with the government of the Philippines at the appropriate time.”
Students and progressive groups have staged several protests against the proposed initiative ahead of Trump's arrival in the Philippines on Tuesday, November 17.
Malacañang, meanwhile, urged students to submit a position paper and discuss their concerns with the government regarding the proposed Pax Silica initiative with the United States.

Earlier this month, the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) said there was no specific date yet for the signing of the legal framework for the planned Pax Silica initiative, which was initially targeted for November, coinciding with Trump's visit to the Philippines.

An official from the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), meanwhile, said the legal framework for Pax Silica was still expected to be signed by the Philippine and US governments before the end of 2026.
Lazaro also said President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and other members of the Philippine delegation had not discussed the protests amid the ASEAN Summit.

“No. The ASEAN was talking about regional issues. The President or no one from the Philippine delegation is talking about anything domestic,” she said when asked whether concerns had been raised about the protests.— MCG, GMA News
